Mount Saint Helens. An active stratovolcano located in Skamania County, Washington, Mount Saint Helens is part of the Cascade Volcanic Arc. It is famous for its catastrophic eruption on May 18, 1980, which stands as the deadliest and most economically destructive volcanic event in United States history. The eruption was triggered by a five point one magnitude earthquake that caused the volcano's entire unstable northern flank to slide away. The mountain experienced a massive lateral blast that blew sideways out of the collapsing mountain, destroying 230 square miles of forest and creating a horseshoe-shaped crater. Prior to the 1980 eruption, the volcano developed a prominent northern bulge, called the Goat Rocks bulge, which grew outward at a rate of up to five feet per day due to rising magma. The eruption lethally trapped U.S. Geological Survey volcanologist David A. Johnston, who radioed his final words from his observation post just before being swept away, saying Vancouver! Vancouver! This is it! Mount Saint Helens is part of the Cascade Volcanic Arc, a segment of the Pacific Ring of Fire named by British explorer George Vancouver after diplomat Alleyne Fitzherbert, first Baron Saint Helens. The volcano connects to Vesuvius, a peer stratovolcano known for Plinian eruptions and pyroclastic flows, and to Mauna Loa, a Hawaiian shield volcano representing a contrasting, effusive eruption style.
